solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Source of funds may determine what this musician plays (5)

definitions.text: Source of funds may determine what this musician plays

blocks.note: the surface reads like arts funding; the setter means a proverb about whoever pays getting to choose
the thing chosen is the tune, and the proverb names the musician whose tune is paid for

explanation.surface: A remark on how whoever pays for the music gets to choose it.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue leans on the proverb 'he who pays the piper calls the tune': the funder picks the tune, so the musician in question is the piper.
explanation.definitionFit: A piper is a musician who plays the pipes, and the proverb makes him the one whose tune is bought.

clue.text: Exam result that is about Victor not working (7)

indicators.note: IE goes about, i.e. around, V

blocks.note: a pass is an exam result
Victor is V in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A student's exam result, somehow connected to a man called Victor who has stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: Victor looks like a person's name, but it is the radio code word for the letter V, which sits inside IE.
explanation.definitionFit: Passive means inert or inactive, which is not working.

clue.text: Topical note is redrafted for Nick (6,7)

indicators.note: a redrafted text has its words rearranged

blocks.note: also fodder, doubling as part of the indicator phrase

explanation.surface: A journalist rewriting a timely note for a colleague called Nick.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick reads as a man's name; in British slang 'the nick' is a police station (and also a prison).
explanation.definitionFit: Nick is British slang for a police station, as in 'taken down the nick'.

clue.text: Never once reorganised to meet again (9)

indicators.note: reorganising puts the letters in a new order

explanation.surface: A committee that was never once reorganised so it could meet again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reorganised' sits comfortably with meetings and committees, which disguises it as part of the story rather than an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: RE- (again) plus CONVENE (come together), used of a meeting resuming after a break.

clue.text: Musician very confused about instrument at the outset (7)

indicators.note: LOST goes about, around, the I

explanation.surface: A musician thoroughly bewildered by an instrument right at the start of the piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very confused' reads as a single phrase, and 'confused' looks like an anagram signal; here it is a plain synonym, bewildered.
explanation.definitionFit: A soloist is a musician who performs alone.

clue.text: Son playing tunes — daily event (6)

indicators.note: the letters of TUNES are played about with

blocks.note: s = son, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A son who plays music every day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing tunes' is exactly what a musical son would do, which hides that 'playing' shuffles the five letters of tunes.
explanation.definitionFit: The sun sets once a day, so sunset is a daily event.

clue.text: Was first seen in double date (3)

indicators.note: the answer can be seen inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the last two letters of 'double' and the first of 'date'

explanation.surface: Someone who showed up first on a double date.
explanation.walkthrough: doub(LE D)ate: the answer straddles the gap between the two words, which is why it is easy to miss.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of lead: a runner who led a race was first, out in front.

clue.text: With no thought for others during argument against team grade (13)

indicators.note: IN = during, as in 'in the war'

blocks.note: the cons are the arguments against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: Someone selfishly holding forth during a row about how a team should be graded.
explanation.walkthrough: The four pieces simply line up in order; 'argument against' is one piece, not two.
explanation.definitionFit: Inconsiderate means thoughtless of other people's feelings or needs.

clue.text: Call time at school (4)

blocks.note: a verb: to call something by a name, to label it
the school year is split into three of these in Britain

explanation.surface: Calling time on the school day.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a bell ringing at school; in fact 'Call' is a verb meaning name, and school time is a term.
explanation.definitionFit: To term something is to call it by a name; a school term is a stretch of teaching time.

clue.text: Element initially seen in layers, one much admired (7)

indicators.note: take the first letter of each of the next words

blocks.note: first letters of Seen In Layers
an icon is an idol, one much admired

explanation.surface: A chemical element first noticed in rock strata, and much admired for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seen in layers' reads like geology, but 'initially' takes the first letter of all three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: silicon (Si, number 14) is one of the chemical elements, the stuff of computer chips.

clue.text: Doctor welcoming environmentally friendly furnishing style (5)

indicators.note: DR welcomes ECO in, holding it inside

explanation.surface: A doctor keen on a green style of home furnishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Welcoming' reads as friendliness towards the style, but it is the containment instruction; ECO is a standard prefix worth knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Decor is the style in which a room is furnished and decorated.

clue.text: Furious, referring to South American empire decline (12)

blocks.note: Incan = of the Inca empire of Peru

explanation.surface: Someone enraged by the fall of a South American empire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Referring to' turns the empire into an adjective: INCA becomes INCAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Incandescent means glowing with heat, and figuratively white-hot with rage.

clue.text: Publican is tersely checking metal containers? (9)

indicators.note: to check is to hold back or contain, so the words hold the answer

blocks.note: the last three letters of 'Publican', all of 'is', and the first four of 'tersely'

explanation.surface: A landlord curtly inspecting the metal kegs in the cellar.
explanation.walkthrough: publi(CAN IS TERS)ely. The question mark flags that 'containers' is also the job the clue words themselves do: they contain the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Canisters are round metal containers, for tea, film or gas.

clue.text: Less difficult exams aid Earl regularly (6)

indicators.note: take letters at regular intervals, every other one

blocks.note: E x A m S a I d E a R l: first, third, fifth letters and so on

explanation.surface: An earl whose exams were made easier by some help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aid' looks like help for the earl in his exams, but it is just part of the letter string.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the comparative of easy, the opposite of difficult, so 'less difficult' swaps straight in.

clue.text: Popular team serving time (6)

explanation.surface: A popular sports team playing out time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serving time' sounds like tennis or a team seeing out a match; it means being in prison, which is being 'inside'.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: a prisoner is said to be 'inside' for the length of a sentence, which is what serving time means.

clue.text: In from France, handle petition earnestly (7)

blocks.note: to treat = to handle, deal with

explanation.surface: Someone just in from France who handles a petition with great earnestness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In from France' reads as arriving from abroad; it asks for the French word for 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to entreat is to beg or implore, a formal word for an earnest request.

clue.text: Employ engineer over long time (6)

explanation.surface: Hiring an engineer for a long spell.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' places ENG above AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the hiring sense, as in engaging a solicitor or a nanny.

clue.text: Model objectives come together — cope financially (4,4,4)

blocks.note: a make is a model, as of a car

explanation.surface: A fashion model whose goals finally come together as she learns to manage money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' is a noun here, a make of product, not a person on a catwalk.
explanation.definitionFit: To make ends meet is to earn just enough to live on, to cope financially.

clue.text: Bird sound that’s amusing (4)

definitions.note: 'that's amusing' stands for something amusing, as in 'it was a hoot'

blocks.note: informal: a thing or person that is great fun

explanation.surface: An owl's call that someone finds funny.
explanation.walkthrough: A hoot is both the owl's cry and, informally, something or someone very funny.
explanation.definitionFit: An owl's call is a hoot, and a hoot is also informal for something highly amusing.

clue.text: Vegetable, one cut twice, I tucked into (5)

indicators.note: cut off the last letter of ONE
use the shortened word two times
I is tucked into the middle of the pair

explanation.surface: A cook chopping a vegetable, cutting it twice and then tucking in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut twice' looks like chopping an onion, but 'cut' trims ONE to ON and 'twice' gives two copies of ON, with I tucked between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the onion is a bulb vegetable, the base of countless dishes, so 'Vegetable' covers it.

clue.text: Most important thing — bring up cake! (3)

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing up raises the letters, turning them bottom to top

blocks.note: a bun is a small cake

explanation.surface: An exclamation that the key thing is to vomit up a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring up' sounds like being sick; in a down entry it means write the word upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The nub is the central point, the most important part of a matter.

clue.text: Moderate anger on road (7)

indicators.note: in an across clue, A on B puts A after B, so RAGE goes second

explanation.surface: Advice to keep road rage in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moderate anger' reads as an instruction to calm down, with 'Moderate' a verb; the definition is the adjective, meaning middling.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something average or moderate is middling, neither high nor low.

clue.text: Credible figure having the necessary skills (7)

blocks.note: ten is a figure, a number

explanation.surface: A believable person who has all the skills needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' looks like a person, but here it is a number.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenable position or argument is one that can be held or believed.

clue.text: Despatched, we hear, for Cologne, maybe (5)

indicators.note: the answer is said like the word before

blocks.note: despatched = sent off, like a letter; say it out loud and respell it

explanation.surface: A parcel posted to the German city of Cologne.
explanation.walkthrough: Cologne looks like the German city, but here it is eau de Cologne, a perfume; 'maybe' marks it as one example of scent.
explanation.definitionFit: Cologne is a light perfume, a kind of scent.
